newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi ready to work against terrorism.
newsitem.headline: Saudi ready to work against terrorism.

text.p: Saudi Arabia was determined to fight terrorism and ready to cooperate with any country for that purpose, Saudi Interior Minister Prince Nayef said.
The official Saudi Press Agency said late on Monday that Prince Nayef made his comments at the end of a meeting of Gulf Arab interior ministers in the Omani capital Muscat.

"We in the kingdom will fight terrorism," he said and added that Saudi Arabia will cooperate with "any country that wants to cooperate with us...in exchanging information or cooperating over security matters".
"The United States is concerned with this because the victims of the two bombings in Khobar and Riyadh were American citizens," he added.
A November 1995 bomb in the capital Riyadh killed five Americans and two Indians, while a truck bombing in June in the eastern town of Khobar killed 19 U.S. airmen.
Four Saudis who confessed on Saudi state-television to being behind the November blast said they were influenced by Islamic groups outside the kingdom. They were later beheaded.
Media reports in the United States had indicated that Washington was not satisfied with Saudi cooperation in connection with the June bombing.
Prince Nayef on Sunday played down reports that Saudi Arabia had arrested some 40 Saudis for the June bombing, saying Saudi security officials were the only credible source of news.
